434-the-circular-staircase.creator: Mary Roberts Rinehart
434-the-circular-staircase.description: A book by Mary Roberts Rinehart. look back over the months I spent at Sunnyside, I wonder that I survived at all. As it is, I show the wear and tear of my harrowing experiences. I have turned very gray—Liddy reminded me of it, only yesterday, by saying that a little bluing in the rinse-water would make my hair silvery, instead of a yellowish white.

73056-the-gospel-of-freedom.title: Gospel Of Freedom
73056-the-gospel-of-freedom.creator: Robert Herrick
73056-the-gospel-of-freedom.description: A book by Robert Herrick. ee, don’t you, Miss Anthon,” his voice was persuasively patronizing, “what I have tried to do? You grasp the difficulties, don’t you? Of course to the crowd it’s nothing but a modern bath, half full of water, with a young woman in it, whose hair is red. But you see the vigor of that leg, the coolness of that water shot with light. The artist--and the rare person--will stop before that picture; _he_ will know what it means.

arxiv-2011-11881.title: A new technique to establish the uniformity of the induction gap in GEM based detector
arxiv-2011-11881.creator: Mohit Gola, F. Brunbauer, D. Janssens, A. Kumar, M. Lisowska, H. Muller, Md. Naimuddin, E. Oliveri, D. Pfeiffer, L. Ropelewski, L. Scharenberg, M. Van Stenis, A. Utrobicic, R. Veenhof
arxiv-2011-11881.description: Abstract This work is proposing and exploring the use of multichannel readout electronics, already used in quality assurance for gain uniformity studies, to measure the uniformity of the induction gap in GEM based detectors. The measurement will furthermore provide a qualification of the readout electrodes in terms of disconnected or shorted channels.

arxiv-2102-12603.title: Crystalline Solutions of Kohn-Sham Equations in the Fractional Quantum Hall Regime
arxiv-2102-12603.creator: Yayun Hu, Yang Ge, Jian-Xiao Zhang, J. K. Jain
arxiv-2102-12603.description: Abstract A Kohn-Sham density functional approach has recently been developed for the fractional quantum Hall effect, which maps the strongly interacting electrons into a system of weakly interacting composite fermions subject to an exchange correlation potential as well as a density dependent gauge field that mimics the “flux quanta” bound to composite fermions.

arxiv-2111-09485.title: 3D Lip Event Detection via Interframe Motion Divergence at Multiple Temporal Resolutions
arxiv-2111-09485.creator: Jie Zhang, Robert B. Fisher
arxiv-2111-09485.description: Abstract The lip is a dominant dynamic facial unit when a person is speaking. Detecting lip events is beneficial to speech analysis and support for the hearing impaired. This paper proposes a 3D lip event detection pipeline that automatically determines the lip events from a 3D speaking lip sequence.

arxiv-2204-05813.title: Explicit models of motions to understand protein side-chain dynamics
arxiv-2204-05813.creator: Nicolas Bolik-Coulon, Olivier Languin-Cattoën, Diego Carnevale, Milan Zachrdla, Damien Laage, Fabio Sterpone, Guillaume Stirnemann, Fabien Ferrage
arxiv-2204-05813.description: Abstract Nuclear magnetic relaxation is widely used to probe protein dynamics. For decades, most analyses of relaxation in proteins have relied successfully on the model-free approach, forgoing mechanistic descriptions of motions. Model-free types of correlation functions cannot describe a large carbon-13 relaxation dataset in protein sidechains.

arxiv-2211-13672.title: A Self-Attention Ansatz for Ab-initio Quantum Chemistry
arxiv-2211-13672.creator: Ingrid von Glehn, James S. Spencer, David Pfau
arxiv-2211-13672.description: Abstract We present a novel neural network architecture using self-attention, the Wavefunction Transformer (Psiformer), which can be used as an approximation (or Ansatz ) for solving the many-electron Schrödinger equation, the fundamental equation for quantum chemistry and material science. This equation can be solved from first principles , requiring no external training data.

arxiv-2308-01571.title: Branching random walks with regularly varying perturbations
arxiv-2308-01571.creator: Krzysztof Kowalski
arxiv-2308-01571.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Krzysztof Kowalski. We consider a modification of classical branching random walk, where we add i.i.d. perturbations to the positions of the particles in each generation. In this model, which was introduced and studied by Bandyopadhyay and Ghosh (2023), perturbations take form 1 θ ​ log ⁡ X E \frac{1}{\theta}\log\frac{X}{E} , where θ \theta is a positive parameter, X X has arbitrary distribution μ \mu and E E is exponential with parameter 1, independent of X X .

arxiv-2310-15133.title: First measurements of in-jet fragmentation and correlations of charmed mesons and baryons in pp collisions with ALICE
arxiv-2310-15133.description: Abstract Fragmentation functions are one of the key components of the factorisation theorem used to calculate heavy-flavour hadron production cross sections. The non-perturbative nature of fragmentation functions necessitates that they are constrained through experimental measurements, commonly performed in the clean environments of e + ​ e − \mathrm{e}^{+}\mathrm{e}^{-} and ep collisions.

arxiv-2312-03903.title: Adaptive Dependency Learning Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2312-03903.creator: Abishek Sriramulu, Nicolas Fourrier, Christoph Bergmeir
arxiv-2312-03903.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNN) have recently gained popularity in the forecasting domain due to their ability to model complex spatial and temporal patterns in tasks such as traffic forecasting and region-based demand forecasting. Most of these methods require a predefined graph as input, whereas in real-life multivariate time series problems, a well-predefined dependency graph rarely exists.

arxiv-2402-18006.title: Characterisation of birefringence inhomogeneity of KAGRA sapphire mirrors from transmitted wavefront error measurements
arxiv-2402-18006.creator: Haoyu Wang, Yoichi Aso, Matteo Leonardi, Marc Eisenmann, Eiichi Hirose, GariLynn Billingsley, Keiko Kokeyama, Takafumi Ushiba, Masahide Tamaki, Yuta Michimura
arxiv-2402-18006.description: Abstract Cooling down test masses to cryogenic temperatures is a way to reduce the thermal noise of gravitational wave detectors. Crystalline materials are considered the most promising materials for fabricating cryogenic test masses and their coatings because of their excellent thermal and optical properties at low temperatures.

arxiv-2405-10074.title: Planning and optimizing transit lines
arxiv-2405-10074.creator: Marie Schmidt University Würzburg, Würzburg, Germany
arxiv-2405-10074.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marie Schmidt University Würzburg, Würzburg, Germany. Abstract For all line-based transit systems like bus, metro and tram, the routes of the lines and the frequencies at which they are operated are determining for the operational performance of the system. However, as transit line planning happens early in the planning process, it is not straightforward to predict the effects of line planning decisions on relevant performance indicators.

arxiv-2408-09598.title: Anytime-Valid Inference for Double/Debiased Machine Learning of Causal Parameters
arxiv-2408-09598.creator: Abhinandan Dalal, Patrick Blöbaum, Shiva Kasiviswanathan, Aaditya Ramdas
arxiv-2408-09598.description: Abstract Double (debiased) machine learning (DML) has seen widespread use in recent years for learning causal/structural parameters, in part due to its flexibility and adaptability to high-dimensional nuisance functions as well as its ability to avoid bias from regularization or overfitting.

arxiv-2501-01958.title: A Survey on Food Ingredient Substitutions
arxiv-2501-01958.creator: Hyunwook Kim, Revathy Venkataramanan, Amit Sheth
arxiv-2501-01958.description: Abstract Diet plays a crucial role in managing chronic conditions and overall well-being. As people become more selective about their food choices, finding recipes that meet dietary needs is important. Ingredient substitution is key to adapting recipes for dietary restrictions, allergies, and availability constraints.

arxiv-2509-23187.title: The characteristics of circular motion and quasiperiodic oscillations around accelerating black hole
arxiv-2509-23187.creator: Tao-Tao Sui a, Xin-Yang Wang a
arxiv-2509-23187.description: Abstract This study explores the motion of massive test particles and associated quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) around an accelerating black hole. The acceleration factor A A suppresses the radial effective potential V eff V_{\text{eff}} , thereby lowering the energy ℰ \mathcal{E} and angular momentum ℒ \mathcal{L} required for stable circular orbits.

pmc-11387897.creator: Andre J. Rowe, Emily J. Rayfield
pmc-11387897.description: SummaryTyrannosauroids are a clade of theropod dinosaur taxa that varied greatly in their body size distribution. We investigated the feeding performance of six tyrannosaur genera of variable body size and skull morphology. We used 3D finite element analysis to test whether skull shape becomes more or less resistant to feeding-induced forces.

pmc-13331205.description: AimsCardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) parameters are used for heart failure (HF) prognostication. While the ventilation to carbon dioxide production (VE/VCO2) slope ≥34 identifies high risk, patients with intermediate values remain heterogeneous. The VE/VCO2 Y-intercept, reflecting dead space ventilation at rest and its changes during effort, may refine prognostication.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed 2642 HF. Follow-up was 26 (9–63) months.
